r21b-2-007.gate_key: rep_questions | B1.2 | gap | At school, years ago: 'Do you like jazz?' → He asked me ___. |

accepted: if I liked jazz or not
whether I liked jazz or not
whether or not I liked jazz

item.q: At school, years ago: 'Do you like jazz?' → He asked me ___.
item.why: After a past reporting verb (*said, told, asked*) the tense goes one step back (*am → was, will → would, have done → had done*). This is always correct. While something is still true, the present is also heard in everyday English, but here we practise the rule.
item.why_lv: Pēc atstāstījuma darbības vārda pagātnē (*said, told, asked*) laiks iet soli atpakaļ (*am → was, will → would, have done → had done*). Tas vienmēr ir pareizi. Kamēr kaut kas joprojām ir patiess, sarunvalodā dzird arī tagadni, bet šeit mēs trenējam likumu.
answers: if I liked jazz or not
whether I liked jazz or not
whether or not I liked jazz

r21b-2-008.gate_key: rep_questions | B1.2 | match | Match each sentence with its report. | 'Please sit down.' = She asked me to sit down. ; 'Don't touch the screen.' = She told me not to touch the screen. ; 'Are you free on Friday?' = She asked me if I was free on Friday. ; 'What time does the train leave?' = She asked me what time the train left.

She asked me if I was free on Friday.

item.q: Match each sentence with its report.

item.why_lv: Lūgumi un rīkojumi: *asked / told* + cilvēks + (*not*) *to*: *She told me not to touch the screen.* Jautājumi: *asked* + *if* vai jautājamais vārds + stāstījuma vārdu secība, laiks vienu soli atpakaļ: *She asked me what time the train left.*
pairs: She asked me to sit down.
She told me not to touch the screen.
She asked me if I was free on Friday.
She asked me what time the train left.
